tldr: NVIDIA research published SWE-Serve on Sep 24, a benchmark for agentic engineering on production inference serving. InfoQ then previewed QCon San Francisco 2026 sessions and ran a platform-engineering case study on LLM hallucinations.
whats_new: InfoQ's Oct 6 preview of QCon London 2027 lists 15 tracks, including agent evaluation and guardrails alongside AI-era architecture and distributed-system debugging.
why_it_matters: These are four loosely related signals, not one event: agent production readiness is increasingly framed as platform engineering, with evals and guardrails now conference-track topics.

beats.headline: SWE-Serve benchmarks agentic engineering for inference serving
QCon SF 2026 lineup centers on operating production systems with AI
Hallucination fix framed as a platform-infrastructure concern
QCon London 2027 adds agent evaluation and guardrails tracks

open_questions: Do other labs or vendors publish results on SWE-Serve?
Do the QCon SF 2026 talks publish concrete production postmortems for agent systems?
Do the QCon London 2027 evaluation and guardrails sessions name specific agent failure modes and fixes?
take_for_builders: Read the InfoQ article's platform controls for hallucination handling and compare them with your own agent guardrails; treat the thread as thin until more sources join.
